reviewedBy: Claude (Opus 5), session 57b768fe, reading the /api/capture?draft output with Jacob Kennedy
source: bookmarklet capture via the Woo Store API, 23 of 24 products
review: THE DRAFT'S PROPOSAL WAS WRONG HERE AND WOULD HAVE COST 18 OF 23 PRODUCTS. It proposed include: ['Custom Chair','Cyberpunk','Kawaii'] because analyse() never proposes the '(none)' bucket. But 18 of the 23 products are untyped, and a non-empty include list drops every untyped product. The shop would have shipped five chairs out of twenty-three and nothing would have said so.
Empty include instead, so all 23 are carried and the classifier places them. 22 land in battlestation and one in arcade, which is fine: it is a chair themed on an arcade cabinet.
One product short of the sitemap's 24. Whatever it is, the live scrape reads the shop directly rather than replaying this capture, so it will be picked up if it is still listed.
Every chair is 419 to 530 dollars. Worth knowing: this merchant will dominate the top of a price-sorted Battlestation shelf.
